links.outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate of retrieval-grounded RAG vs general LLMs on DLBCL questions
links.effect: RAG had highest mean accuracy (2.46 vs GPT-4 2.26, GPT-3.5 1.82, Prometheus 1.74) and fewest answers with hallucinations (3/19 vs GPT-3.5 13/19, GPT-4 8/19).
links.quote: Overall, the RAG model enhanced with domain specific data outperformed other LLMs with respect to accuracy and relevance of answers, and produced answers with the fewest observed hallucinations.

links.outcome: Fabricated or incorrect references in generative AI outputs
links.effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 gave numerical response rates inconsistent with cited references, with fabricated or incorrect references; GPT models had hallucinations in 13/19 and 8/19 answers.
links.quote: Numerical overall and complete response rates (ORR and CRR, respectively) reported by GPT-3.5 (ORR = 65.1%, CRR = 35.1%) and GPT-4 (ORR = 62.7%, CRR = 39.2%) were not consistent with their references cited and had either fabricated or provided incorrect references.

links.outcome: Outdated knowledge from training cutoff and incomplete retrieval corpus affecting answers
links.effect: RAG answer to glofitamab response rate question was inaccurate because the key trial paper was not in the corpus; GPT models trained only up to September 2021.
links.quote: The RAG model result was not accurate in answering this question because the official glofitamab trial efficacy paper [ 36 ] was not available on PubMed Central ( https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/ ) and therefore not included in the corpus.

links.outcome: grounded RAG answer accuracy and hallucinations
links.effect: RAG accuracy averaged 2.46 versus GPT-4 2.26, GPT-3.5 1.82, Prometheus 1.74; hallucinations were RAG 3/19 versus GPT-4 8/19, GPT-3.5 13/19, Prometheus 4/19.
links.quote: Overall, the RAG model enhanced with domain specific data outperformed other LLMs with respect to accuracy and relevance of answers, and produced answers with the fewest observed hallucinations.

links.effect: Average accuracy scores: RAG 2.46, GPT-4 2.26, GPT-3.5 1.82, Prometheus 1.74; high-accuracy questions were 12/19, 7/19, 2/19, and 4/19 respectively.
links.quote: Across the 19 questions tested, the RAG model had the highest average score (2.46), followed by GPT-4 (2.26), GPT-3.5 (1.82), and Prometheus (1.74) ( Fig 1A ).

links.effect: Answers with ≥1 hallucination: GPT-3.5 13/19, GPT-4 8/19, Prometheus 4/19, RAG 3/19; hallucinations primarily fabricated references and clinical results.
links.quote: These hallucinations were primarily associated with fabrication of both references and clinical results.

links.effect: For question #13, retrieval returned multiple myeloma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia articles rather than DLBCL material, and the summarizer produced an incorrect answer.
links.quote: For example, question #13 asked about minimal residual disease (MRD) in DLBCL, but the document retriever returned articles about MRD in multiple myeloma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia—two distinct hematological malignancies from DLBCL.

links.outcome: missing trial paper in retrieval corpus
links.effect: For the glofitamab ORR question, RAG was inaccurate because the official trial efficacy paper was unavailable on PubMed Central and absent from its corpus.
links.quote: The RAG model result was not accurate in answering this question because the official glofitamab trial efficacy paper [ 36 ] was not available on PubMed Central ( https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/ ) and therefore not included in the corpus.
